blocks.text: Haemoglobin is a protein present in RBCs. A haemoglobin molecule is composed of four globin (globular) polypeptide chains (two α chains and two β) and four haem groups. There are 141 and 146 amino acids in the α and β chains, respectively. Each polypeptide chain is folded in such a way that it contains a pocket where the heme group binds. So, each chain is associated with a haem group. A haem group consists of an iron ion held in a porphyrin ring. The iron ion is attached with four nitrogen atoms of the polypeptide chain. Under higher partial pressure of oxygen, iron ion attaches a molecule of O₂. In this way, one haemoglobin molecule can carry up to four O₂ molecules.
book_errors: four nitrogen atoms of the polypeptide chain

blocks.text: The four polypeptide chains of haemoglobin are bound to each other by salt bridges, hydrogen bonds, and hydrophobic effect.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The four nitrogen atoms that hold the iron ion belong to the porphyrin ring of the haem group, not to the polypeptide chain.
